title: Clamshell Packaging: History & Overview
content: # The History of Clamshell Packaging. Clamshell packaging is a form of plastic blister packaging that was first developed in 1978 by U.S. inventor Thomas Jake Lunsford. The term “blister packaging” refers to pre-formed plastic containers that are commonly used for packaging products such as pharmaceuticals, office supplies, electronics, hardware, and cosmetics. A blister pack typically includes a pocket made from thermoformed plastic that securely holds the product, providing protection and visibility. The clamshell package, named for its resemblance to the shell of a clam), is a type of blister pack characterized by a hinged design. It consists of a single piece of plastic that forms both the top and bottom sections, connected by a thin, flexible hinge. This hinge, made from the same material as the two rigid halves, allows the package to open and close seamlessly, providing functional packaging without the need for separate components. The clamshell’s pocket is custom-molded to fit the product’s shape, offering a secure hold and a visually appealing display.
